transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I came in because I’ve been having these thoughts, and they scared me. Like, I keep thinking maybe my family would be better off if I didn’t wake up. I know that sounds bad saying it out loud.

I told my supervisor, actually. He’s the one who said I should come in. We were at work and I was trying to just keep moving like normal, you know, because there’s always something breaking down or somebody needing something, and I’ve been doing that kind of work a long time… but that thought just kept sitting there. So, yeah, that’s why I’m here.
Have you had thoughts about death or wanting not to live before this recent incident at work, or has this been happening more often?

Yeah… I mean, I can’t say it was just that one day. It’s been coming up more, that thought about, you know, maybe my family would be better off if I didn’t wake up. I don’t like even saying it.

At work I usually just stay busy—there’s always some machine acting up or somebody asking where something is, and I try to keep my head down and handle it—but that thought kept hanging around. That’s what scared me enough that I finally told my supervisor.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore—like activities you used to enjoy or even spending time with family?

Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. I used to be out there messing with my tomato plants, checking them like they were something important, you know? And I had my little bench where I’d sand wood, just kind of work with my hands.

On Sundays I’d watch the Falcons, and after church I’d stand around talking longer than I needed to—sometimes my wife would have to give me that look like, come on, let’s go. But lately… I don’t know. I look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. Like it’s sitting there, but I can’t get myself to care much about it.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual or noticed that you don’t have the energy to do things you normally would?

I don’t know… I mean, I’m 57, so some days I figure tired just comes with the package, you know? Work wears a man down after enough years. There’s always a crew needing something or some problem you’re supposed to fix before anybody else notices it.

But as far as, like, a clear change… I’m not sure I could say. I still get up and do what I’m supposed to do, mostly. My wife might tell you different, I guess, but I don’t really keep track of it like that.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately, like waking up earlier than you'd like or having a hard time falling asleep?

I don’t really know how to answer that clean. Some nights I’m in bed, but whether I’m sleeping good… I couldn’t tell you exactly.

My wife says I move around, but she also says that about the dog when he gets on the bed, so I don’t know. I’ve never been one of those people who falls asleep the second their head hits the pillow. Even back when the kids were little, I’d be listening for every little sound in the house.

Lately… I guess I haven’t paid close enough attention to say if it’s worse. I’m not sure.
Have you noticed that you react less to things that used to make you happy or upset, like you don’t feel emotions as strongly as before?

Yeah… I guess that’s one way to put it. It’s like I know I ought to feel something, but it doesn’t really catch like it used to.

Like those tomato plants I used to fool with—I’d be out there checking them, tying them up, fussing over whether they needed water. And I had that bench where I’d sand wood, just kind of get lost in it. Sundays, I’d watch the Falcons, and after church I’d stand around talking to folks forever. My wife used to have to nudge me along.

Now I see all that sitting there and it’s like… I don’t know, like it belongs to somebody else. Like those were my things, but they don’t pull at me the same.
Have you ever had a period of time before this where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. Looking back, it’s not like it just started yesterday. These low stretches have been coming around for maybe about a year now, off and on.

I didn’t really call it anything at the time. I’d just say I was worn out, or work was getting to me, or it was just one of those weeks. But this one… after my daughter left, this one’s been the hardest. It’s stuck around more than the others, I guess.
Before this most recent period of feeling down, did you ever have a time when you felt low or lost interest in things for at least a couple of weeks?

Yeah… yeah, before this one, I think there were times like that. Not always real obvious to me while I was in it, you know? I’d just figure I was tired or had too much on my plate.

Looking back, though, those low stretches have been showing up for maybe about a year now. They’d come and go. But this one, after my daughter left… that’s the one that really knocked me down the hardest. It’s felt heavier than the others.
Has this most recent period of feeling down lasted for more than two years, or is it something that started more recently within the past two years?

No, not two years. This... this really changed about two weeks ago, when my daughter left Georgia for the military.

I mean, I keep thinking about the day she left, and then I’ll start remembering all kinds of things—her packing, me standing around not knowing what to say, the house feeling different after. But the real heaviness, the way I’ve been lately, that’s been these past couple weeks.
Before this most recent low period that started two weeks ago, how often did you experience similar feelings, and how long did they usually last?

Before this one? It’d come and go, I guess… over the last year or so. Like I’d have these stretches where I just felt low, and then I’d sort of pull out of it enough to keep going.

I couldn’t tell you every time exactly how long. Sometimes it felt like a couple weeks, sometimes maybe longer, but I didn’t really keep track. I was busy with work stuff, and there’s always something breaking or somebody needing something, so I’d just push through it.

But this one, after my daughter left… this one’s been different. It’s hit me the hardest.

Before this most recent episode that started after your daughter left, did you have separate periods of feeling down that were followed by times when you felt back to normal before the next low period started?

Yeah, I think so… I mean, looking back, those low stretches have been coming around for maybe about a year. They’d sort of show up, and then I’d get busy with work or something at home and feel more like myself for a while.

It’s funny, you don’t always notice it when you’re in it—like when a machine at work starts making a noise and you just tune it out until it breaks. But yeah, there were separate times, I guess. This one after my daughter left, though… that’s the one that’s hit me the hardest.

Before this most recent episode that started after your daughter left, did you have at least two other separate times where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had similar symptoms that lasted for at least a couple of weeks each?

Yeah… looking back, those low stretches have been coming around for about a year. I don’t know if I could count them cleanly, like “this one started here and ended there,” you know? Life doesn’t put lines around it like that.

There were a few times before this, I think, where I’d get down for a while and then kind of come back up enough to function. Work would pick up, or something at the house would need fixing, and I’d just get pulled along. But this one after my daughter left… this one’s been the hardest by far.
Have you completely stopped doing things you used to enjoy, like watching the Falcons or working with your hands, or do you still try to do them even if they don’t feel the same?

I don’t know if I’ve completely stopped, exactly… I mean, the TV’s still there, and my tools are still out in the garage. But it’s like I look at them and they don’t feel like mine.

I used to mess with my tomato plants, you know, check them after work, pull the bad leaves off. I’d sand wood at my bench just to have my hands doing something. Falcons game would be on and I’d holler at the TV like that was gonna help ’em any. And after church I used to hang around talking to folks.

Lately I just kind of look at all that like it belongs to somebody else. I might sit there, but I’m not really in it.
Before the low periods you described over the last year, was there ever a time when you felt completely back to normal—like your old self—before the next low period started?

I’m not real sure. There were times I thought I was doing better, like I’d get up and go to work and talk normal, get things done around the house. But “completely back to my old self”… I don’t know.

It’s hard to tell, because when you’re working every day, you just kind of keep moving. Like at the plant, if things are running, you don’t stop and ask if every belt and bearing sounds perfect—you just keep the line going. So maybe I was better between them, but I don’t know if I ever sat there and thought, “Yep, I’m fully back.”
